question: Let $f(t)=t^3-2t$ and $g(x)=\sin(x^2+1)$, and define $h=f\circ g$. Using the chain rule, determine $h'(x)$ in simplified form and hence obtain the exact value of $h'(1)$.
explanation:
Formation of the Composite Function
Since $h=f\circ g$, we have $$h(x)=f(g(x)).$$ With $f(t)=t^3-2t$ and $g(x)=\sin(x^2+1)$, $$h(x)=\sin^3(x^2+1)-2\sin(x^2+1).$$

Applying the Chain Rule
For a composite function $h(x)=f(g(x))$, the chain rule gives $$h'(x)=f'(g(x))\,g'(x).$$ Now, $$f'(t)=3t^2-2.$$ Therefore, $$f'(g(x))=3\sin^2(x^2+1)-2.$$

Also, differentiating $g(x)=\sin(x^2+1)$ by the chain rule, $$g'(x)=\cos(x^2+1)\frac{d}{dx}(x^2+1)=2x\cos(x^2+1).$$ Hence, $$h'(x)=\left[3\sin^2(x^2+1)-2\right]\left[2x\cos(x^2+1)\right].$$ Thus, $$h'(x)=2x\cos(x^2+1)\left[3\sin^2(x^2+1)-2\right].$$

Evaluation at $x=1$
Substituting $x=1$, we get $$h'(1)=2\cos2\left(3\sin^22-2\right).$$

Final Result
Therefore, $$h'(x)=2x\cos(x^2+1)\left[3\sin^2(x^2+1)-2\right]$$ and $$h'(1)=2\cos2\left(3\sin^22-2\right).$$
